answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake of earned reputation as collateral, turning the stake into a costly signal that spawning many fake identities multiplies expense instead of reward. Like a trellis that admits only one vine per opening, the network routes payments and votes through a single attested channel per stake, exposing duplicates for cheap pruning. Honest work grows the stake over time, and a crystal-clear audit trail lets peers verify each identity's history is real, making fakes expensive to build and easy to catch.
